approachQuestion.prompt:
Repack the Display

A rectangular integer matrix grid has r rows and c columns. Produce a new matrix with a rows and b columns containing exactly the same sequence obtained by reading grid row by row, left to right. If the number of cells differs, return null. A valid result must have fresh, distinct row arrays and must not share row storage with grid.

Example 1: grid = [[8,3,5],[1,9,2]], a = 3, b = 2 → [[8,3],[5,1],[9,2]].
Example 2: grid = [[4,7]], a = 1, b = 3 → null.
Example 3: grid = [[6],[6]], a = 1, b = 2 → [[6,6]].

Constraints:
1 ≤ r, c, a, b ≤ 200,000; r*c and a*b are each at most 200,000.
Every row of grid has length c; −10^9 ≤ each value ≤ 10^9.
Do not modify grid. Indices start at zero. Return either the new matrix or null.
constraints: 1 ≤ r, c, a, b ≤ 200,000; r*c and a*b are each at most 200,000.
Every row of grid has length c; −10^9 ≤ each value ≤ 10^9.
Do not modify grid. Indices start at zero. Return either the new matrix or null.

options.text: Reject unequal cell counts. Otherwise allocate fresh output rows. For each position k from 0 through r*c−1, copy grid[k div c][k mod c] to result[k div b][k mod b].
options.feedback: A linear position identifies the same element before and after repacking. The old column count decodes the source, and the new column count decodes the destination.

options.text: Reject unequal cell counts. Otherwise flatten all input cells into a separate temporary array, then fill fresh output rows from that array.
options.feedback: This preserves every value and its order, but the temporary flat copy is removable: source indices can be decoded directly.

options.text: Reject unequal cell counts. Otherwise transpose grid and return it, regardless of a and b.
options.feedback: Equal area does not mean transposition gives the requested shape or order. Example 1 needs three rows of two, but its transpose is [[8,1],[3,9],[5,2]], which has the wrong sequence.

options.text: Reject unequal cell counts. Otherwise create one mutable row array, reuse that same array for every output row, and fill the rows in row order.
options.feedback: The rows must have distinct storage. For grid=[[1,2],[3,4]], a=2,b=2, filling the second reused row also overwrites the first, leaving two references to [3,4].

feedback.reason: The linear row-wise position is preserved while its row and column coordinates change.
details: Check the cell counts first. Allocate distinct result rows and copy each value using its position in the row-wise sequence, decoding source and destination with their respective column counts.

The linear row-wise position is preserved while its row and column coordinates change. Equal cell counts are necessary before allocating the new shape. Independent destination rows prevent a write through one row from unexpectedly changing another row through shared storage.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the fixed method “Decode Each Cell Position”, choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Let N=r*c, and analyze compatible shapes (a*b=N). Indexed access, integer division, allocation per cell and assignment have constant cost. Count all copying time. Exclude the input and all returned matrix storage, including row references; include helper variables and call stack. No recursion, hashing or dynamic append is used.
constraints: 1 ≤ r, c, a, b ≤ 200,000; r*c and a*b are each at most 200,000.
Every row of grid has length c; −10^9 ≤ each value ≤ 10^9.
Do not modify grid. Indices start at zero. Return either the new matrix or null.

feedback.reason: Copy N cells once into independently allocated returned rows.
details: Each of the N cells is copied once. Creating a distinct rows also fits within this bound because a≤N. Only indices and shape values remain outside the returned matrix. An incompatible shape can be rejected immediately; the question analyzes compatible shapes.
The option “O(N) time, O(1) auxiliary space.”: This counts every copied cell and excludes only the returned matrix.
The option “O(N) time, O(N) auxiliary space.”: A separate flattened copy would occupy this space, but the fixed method does not create one.
The option “O(1) time, O(1) auxiliary space.”: Fresh output requires writing all N cells; a view is not allowed.
The option “O(N²) time, O(1) auxiliary space.”: Index decoding does not rescan earlier cells.
